title: The Calm Eye of the Storm
author: Mohinish, Dad

blocks.text: The Calm Eye of the Storm

My dear Aadi, some days feel like a big swirly storm. Toys everywhere, everyone talking at once, plans changing, and today it's Halloween too, with costumes and candy and doorbells ringing. This letter is about a secret: a little chaos is not a bad thing. And right in the middle of it, you can find a calm spot to think.
"Chaos is where new things are made. Discipline is how you choose which ones to build."

Chaos means lots of things happening at once, all mixed up, with no neat order. Discipline is a grown-up word for choosing what matters most, and then sticking with it, even when lots of other things are calling your name. You need both.

Stars are born inside huge, messy clouds of gas and dust, called nebulas. A rocket launch is loud, smoky and shaky, and that's exactly what lifting off looks like. A jumbled Lego bin means every piece is ready for something new. Messy can mean something exciting is about to be built.
blocks.heading: Chaos means things are happening

blocks.text: A hurricane is wild and windy, but right in its middle is a quiet, calm circle called the eye. You can make your own eye. Stop, take three slow breaths, and ask yourself one question: "What matters most right now?"
blocks.heading: Find the calm eye of the storm

blocks.text: Imagine a jar, some big rocks, some pebbles and some sand. Pour the sand in first and the big rocks won't fit. Put the big rocks in first, and the pebbles and sand slide in around them. Big rocks are the things that really matter: family, kindness, learning, your big dream. Do them first.
blocks.heading: Put the big rocks in first

blocks.text: It isn't about being strict or grumpy. It's keeping a small promise every day, like brushing your teeth, reading one book, or adding one more floor to your Lego tower. Small promises kept every day become giant things.
blocks.heading: Discipline is a promise to yourself

blocks.text: When you're building, a hundred shiny things will wave at you: a cartoon, a new toy, a noise outside. You don't have to say "never". You can say "not now, after I finish". That tiny sentence is a superpower.
blocks.heading: Say "not now" to shiny things

blocks.text: In 1970, far out in space, the Apollo 13 astronauts radioed, "Houston, we've had a problem." Lots of things were going wrong at once. The team at Mission Control, in the same Houston you visited, didn't try to fix everything. They focused on the one thing that mattered most, getting the crew home safely, and solved it one step at a time. They even worked out how to make a square air filter fit a round hole, using things already on the spaceship. And the astronauts came home.
blocks.heading: Do the next right thing

blocks.text: Not every kind of chaos is fun. When things feel too big, too loud or too scary, the first thing to do is find a grown-up and a hug, and that's a smart choice, not a weak one. Discipline isn't about never playing or never being silly. It's about choosing. Play time is a big rock too.

So here is what I want you to remember, Aadi: the world will always be a little bit messy, and that's okay. The people who do great things are not the ones with no chaos around them. They're the ones who can stand in the middle of it, find the calm eye, pick the thing that really matters, and keep building it, one small step every day. You can do that. I've seen you do it at the Lego table.
Your calm spot in every storm, Dad
